note: Physics round 4: applied and calculation items across all fifteen topics, taking Physics past 500 curated questions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pressure of a gas is measured as 2.5 × 10⁵ N/m². Expressed in fundamental units, N/m² is equivalent to
questions.explanation: N = kg m s⁻², so N/m² = kg m s⁻² ÷ m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylinder has a diameter of 2.0 cm and a length of 10.00 cm. Its volume, quoted to the correct number of significant figures, is
questions.explanation: V = πr²l = π × 1.0² × 10.00 = 31.4 cm³, but the diameter has only two significant figures, so the answer is quoted as 31 cm³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The period of a mass m on a spring of force constant k is T = 2π√(m/k). The unit of k in base SI units is
questions.explanation: Rearranging, k = 4π²m/T², so its unit is kg/s² = kg s⁻² (the same as N/m).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following measurements is recorded to three significant figures?
questions.explanation: In 2.50 the zero after the decimal point is significant, giving three significant figures; the others have two.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To find the thickness of one sheet of paper, a student measures the thickness of a stack of 200 sheets with a vernier caliper and divides by 200. This is done because
questions.A: a single sheet is too thin for the caliper to measure accurately
questions.B: the caliper cannot measure anything shorter than one centimetre
questions.C: a single sheet of paper expands as soon as it is handled
questions.D: a stack of sheets has a smaller zero error than one sheet
questions.explanation: One sheet (about 0.1 mm) is thinner than the caliper's precision; measuring many sheets and dividing spreads the reading error over all of them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stopwatch that runs slow is used to time a 100 m race. The recorded times will be
questions.explanation: A slow watch under-records every interval by the same fraction; the error is always in the same direction, so it is systematic and cannot be removed by averaging.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The density of a liquid is 0.8 g/cm³. In SI units this is
questions.explanation: 1 g/cm³ = 1,000 kg/m³, so 0.8 g/cm³ = 800 kg/m³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular plate has sides measured as 4.0 ± 0.1 cm and 2.0 ± 0.1 cm. The greatest possible value of its area is
questions.explanation: Taking both sides at their maximum values: 4.1 × 2.1 = 8.61 cm².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The wavelength 6.4 × 10⁻⁷ m expressed in nanometres is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student determines g by timing a simple pendulum. Which of the following introduces a systematic error?
questions.A: starting the stopwatch slightly late on some of the swings
questions.B: using a heavier bob on the same length of thread
questions.C: counting the oscillations aloud while timing them
questions.D: measuring the length to the top of the bob instead of to its centre
questions.explanation: Measuring to the wrong point makes every length reading too small by the same amount, shifting all the results in one direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ship sails 30 km due east and then 40 km due north. The bearing of its final position from the starting point is approximately
questions.explanation: tan θ = 30/40 = 0.75, so θ = 37° measured from north towards east: bearing 037°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 50 N acts at 30° to the vertical. Its vertical component is
questions.explanation: Vertical component = 50 cos 30° = 50 × 0.866 = 43.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Forces of 3 N and 4 N act on a particle at right angles to each other, and a third force of 5 N acts in the direction opposite to their resultant. The net force on the particle is
questions.explanation: The resultant of 3 N and 4 N at right angles is 5 N; the third force cancels it exactly, so the particle is in equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An aeroplane heads due north at 200 km/h while a wind blows at 50 km/h towards the east. Its speed over the ground is approximately
questions.explanation: The two velocities are perpendicular: ground speed = √(200² + 50²) = 206 km/h.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tyre gauge reads 2.2 bar, a weighing scale reads 700 N and a signpost says 'Lagos 40 km, north-west'. The reading that is a scalar quantity is the
questions.A: 700 N, since weight always acts vertically
questions.B: 700 N and the 40 km north-west together
questions.C: 40 km north-west, since it names a direction
questions.D: 2.2 bar, since pressure has no direction
questions.explanation: Pressure has magnitude only; weight (a force) and the signpost's displacement both have a direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A delivery rider goes 5 km north to a shop, 5 km east to a second shop and then 5 km south to the customer. The rider's displacement from the starting point is
questions.explanation: The northward and southward legs cancel, leaving only the 5 km eastward leg; the distance walked is 15 km but the displacement is 5 km east.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two vectors have magnitudes 8 units and 6 units. If the magnitude of their sum is 14 units, the angle between them is
questions.explanation: The sum equals 8 + 6 only when the vectors point in the same direction, i.e. the angle between them is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car travels 60 km due north in 1 hour and then returns 60 km due south in the next hour. Its average velocity for the whole journey is
questions.explanation: Average velocity = total displacement ÷ time = 0 ÷ 2 h = 0, although the average speed is 60 km/h.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body moving with uniform speed in a circular path has
questions.C: constant velocity and an acceleration along the tangent
questions.D: changing velocity and an acceleration towards the centre
questions.explanation: The direction of motion changes continuously, so the velocity changes and there is a centripetal acceleration even though the speed is constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boat crosses a river 100 m wide by heading straight across at 2 m/s while the river flows at 1.5 m/s. The distance the boat is carried downstream is
questions.explanation: Crossing time = 100/2 = 50 s; in that time the current carries the boat 1.5 × 50 = 75 m downstream.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resultant of two forces of 12 N and 5 N acting at right angles is balanced by a third force. The magnitude of the third force is
questions.explanation: The resultant is √(12² + 5²) = 13 N, so the balancing force (equilibrant) is also 13 N, in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 100 N acts at 60° to the direction in which a body moves. The component of the force in the direction of motion is
questions.explanation: Component along the motion = 100 cos 60° = 50 N; only this part does work on the body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two tug boats pull a barge with equal forces F, their tow ropes making an angle of 60° with each other. The magnitude of the resultant pull on the barge is
questions.explanation: R² = F² + F² + 2F² cos 60° = 3F², so R = √3 F = 1.73F.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 8 s. The distance it covers during this time is
questions.explanation: Distance = average velocity × time = ½(10 + 30) × 8 = 160 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from the top of a cliff 20 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s², it strikes the ground at a horizontal distance from the foot of the cliff of
questions.explanation: Time of fall t = √(2h/g) = √(40/10) = 2 s; horizontal distance = 15 × 2 = 30 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. The ratio of the distance covered in the first 2 s to the distance covered in the first 4 s is
questions.explanation: s = ½at², so the distances are in the ratio 2² : 4² = 4 : 16 = 1 : 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The displacement–time graph of a body is a straight line inclined to the time axis. The body is
questions.explanation: A constant slope on a displacement–time graph means the displacement changes at a steady rate: uniform velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lift starts from rest and accelerates upwards at 2 m/s² for 3 s, then moves at constant velocity for 5 s. The total distance travelled in the 8 s is
questions.explanation: First stage: s = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 m, reaching v = 6 m/s; second stage: 6 × 5 = 30 m; total 39 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is dropped from a height of 80 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², the distance it falls during the last second of its fall is
questions.explanation: Total time = √(2 × 80/10) = 4 s; distance in the first 3 s = ½ × 10 × 9 = 45 m, so the last second covers 80 − 45 = 35 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude 5 cm and period 2 s. Its maximum speed is approximately
questions.explanation: ω = 2π/T = π rad/s; v_max = Aω = 5 × π = 15.7 cm/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rotates at 120 revolutions per minute. The linear speed of a point on its rim is approximately
questions.explanation: 120 rev/min = 2 rev/s, so ω = 2π × 2 = 4π rad/s and v = rω = 0.5 × 4π = 6.28 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cyclist rides round a circular track of radius 20 m at a constant speed of 10 m/s. His acceleration is
questions.B: 0.5 m/s² towards the centre of the track
questions.C: 5 m/s² along the tangent to the track
questions.D: 5 m/s² towards the centre of the track
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = 100/20 = 5 m/s², always directed towards the centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parachutist falling at terminal velocity opens her parachute. Immediately afterwards she
questions.A: continues to fall at the same speed
questions.B: accelerates because her weight suddenly increases
questions.C: decelerates because the air resistance now exceeds her weight
questions.D: stops falling and hangs motionless in the air
questions.explanation: The open parachute greatly increases the drag; the upward force is now larger than the weight, so she slows until a new, lower terminal velocity is reached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 5 kg is acted on by two opposing forces of 30 N and 10 N along the same line. Its acceleration is
questions.explanation: Net force = 30 − 10 = 20 N; a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform beam 6 m long weighing 300 N rests on supports at its two ends. A 600 N load is placed 2 m from the left end. The reaction at the left support is
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the right end: R × 6 = 300 × 3 + 600 × 4 = 3,300, so R = 550 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tight nut is loosened more easily with a long spanner than with a short one because the longer spanner
questions.A: applies a much larger force directly on the nut
questions.B: has a smaller mass and so is easier to swing
questions.C: produces a larger moment for the same applied force
questions.D: reduces the friction between the nut and its thread
questions.explanation: Moment = force × perpendicular distance; a longer handle gives a bigger turning effect for the same push.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1.5 kg book rests on a horizontal table. Taking g = 10 m/s², the normal reaction of the table on the book is
questions.explanation: The book is in equilibrium, so the upward reaction equals its weight, mg = 1.5 × 10 = 15 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of weight 20 N rests on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The component of its weight acting down the plane is
questions.explanation: Component along the plane = W sin θ = 20 × sin 30° = 10 N; the component into the plane is 20 cos 30° = 17.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The smallest horizontal force needed to start a 60 kg crate sliding on a rough floor is 240 N. Taking g = 10 m/s², the coefficient of static friction is
questions.explanation: μ = limiting friction ÷ normal reaction = 240/(60 × 10) = 0.4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1,000 kg car moving at 20 m/s is stopped by its brakes in 5 s. The average braking force is
questions.explanation: Deceleration = 20/5 = 4 m/s²; F = ma = 1,000 × 4 = 4,000 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 3 kg mass is pulled vertically upwards by a rope with an acceleration of 3 m/s². Taking g = 10 m/s², the tension in the rope is
questions.explanation: T − mg = ma, so T = m(g + a) = 3 × 13 = 39 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy stands on a bathroom scale in a lift that is moving downwards and slowing down. The reading on the scale is
questions.explanation: Slowing down while descending means the acceleration is upwards, so the reaction R = m(g + a) is larger than the weight.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two boys pull on opposite ends of a rope with forces of 200 N each and the rope does not move. The tension in the rope is
questions.explanation: Each end is pulled with 200 N and the rope is in equilibrium; the tension throughout the rope is 200 N, not the sum of the two pulls.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 4 kg mass and a 6 kg mass hang from the ends of a light string passing over a smooth pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s², the acceleration of the masses is
questions.explanation: Net force = (6 − 4) × 10 = 20 N acting on a total mass of 10 kg: a = 20/10 = 2 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light metre rule carries a 40 g mass at the 10 cm mark and a 60 g mass at the 80 cm mark. It balances horizontally on a knife-edge placed at the
questions.explanation: For balance 40(x − 10) = 60(80 − x), so 100x = 5,200 and x = 52 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 60 kg athlete runs up a hill 30 m high in 1 minute. Taking g = 10 m/s², her average power output against gravity is
questions.explanation: Work against gravity = mgh = 60 × 10 × 30 = 18,000 J; power = 18,000/60 = 300 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 0.2 kg ball dropped from a height of 5 m rebounds to a height of 3.2 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², the energy lost in the bounce is
questions.explanation: Energy lost = mg(h₁ − h₂) = 0.2 × 10 × (5 − 3.2) = 3.6 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg block sliding along a horizontal floor at 6 m/s comes to rest after travelling 9 m. The average frictional force on it is
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = ½ × 2 × 6² = 36 J; work done by friction F × 9 = 36, so F = 4 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electricity bill is charged in kilowatt-hours, a physicist quotes photon energies in electron-volts and a food label gives energy in kilojoules. A quantity that these three units can NOT all measure is
questions.explanation: Kilowatt-hour, electron-volt and kilojoule are all units of energy (work or heat); power is energy per second and is measured in watts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A catapult stores 4 J of elastic potential energy and fires a 20 g stone. Ignoring losses, the speed of the stone as it leaves the catapult is
questions.explanation: ½mv² = 4, so v² = 8/0.02 = 400 and v = 20 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A machine lifts a 200 kg load through 5 m in 20 s while taking an input power of 1 kW. Taking g = 10 m/s², the efficiency of the machine is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pump raises water to a tank 10 m above the ground at the rate of 30 kg every minute. Taking g = 10 m/s², the useful power of the pump is
questions.explanation: Work per minute = 30 × 10 × 10 = 3,000 J; power = 3,000/60 = 50 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass m moving with velocity v has kinetic energy E. If its velocity increases to 3v, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to v², so tripling the velocity multiplies the energy by 3² = 9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a moving car is braked to a stop, most of its kinetic energy is converted into
questions.C: heat in the brakes and tyres
questions.explanation: Friction in the brakes and between the tyres and the road turns the kinetic energy into heat.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 500 g toy car is pushed up a smooth slope with an initial speed of 4 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the vertical height it rises before stopping is
questions.explanation: ½mv² = mgh, so h = v²/2g = 16/20 = 0.8 m; the mass cancels.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A generator converts 80% of the mechanical energy supplied to it into electrical energy. To deliver 4 kW of electrical power it must receive mechanical power of
questions.explanation: Input = output ÷ efficiency = 4/0.8 = 5 kW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 3 kg rifle fires a 15 g bullet at 300 m/s. The recoil speed of the rifle is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 3 × v = 0.015 × 300, so v = 1.5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 60 kg man jumps horizontally out of a stationary 240 kg boat at 2 m/s. The boat moves off in the opposite direction at

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 kg body moving at 4 m/s collides head-on with a 3 kg body moving at 2 m/s in the opposite direction. If they stick together, their common speed after the collision is
questions.explanation: Total momentum = 5 × 4 − 3 × 2 = 14 kg m/s shared by 8 kg: v = 14/8 = 1.75 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg hammer moving at 5 m/s strikes a nail and stops in 0.01 s. The average force on the nail is
questions.explanation: F = change in momentum ÷ time = (2 × 5)/0.01 = 1,000 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Seat belts and air bags reduce injury in a car crash mainly because they
questions.A: reduce the change in the passenger's momentum
questions.B: bring the car itself to rest much more quickly
questions.C: increase the force needed to stop the passenger
questions.D: increase the time over which the momentum changes
questions.explanation: The passenger's momentum change is fixed; spreading it over a longer time reduces the average force on the body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block and tackle with 6 pulleys lifts a 900 N load with an effort of 200 N. Its efficiency is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inclined plane 6 m long rises through a height of 1.5 m. A 500 N load is pushed up it with an effort of 200 N. The efficiency of the plane is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lever has its fulcrum 20 cm from the load and 80 cm from the effort. Ignoring friction, the effort needed to lift a 100 N load is
questions.explanation: Effort × 80 = 100 × 20, so the effort is 25 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A screw jack has a pitch of 4 mm and a handle 28 cm long, and is 50% efficient. The effort needed to raise a 4,400 N load is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball bounces off a wall with the same speed at which it arrived. The quantity that is unchanged by the collision is its
questions.explanation: Speed is unchanged so the kinetic energy is unchanged; the velocity and momentum reverse direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following machines has a velocity ratio less than 1?
questions.A: a pair of scissors with long blades and short handles
questions.B: a crowbar with a long handle and a short lifting end
questions.C: a bottle opener with the pivot near the cap
questions.D: a nutcracker with the nut close to the hinge
questions.explanation: With short handles and long blades the blade tips move further than the handles, so the effort moves less than the load: VR < 1 and the machine gains speed, not force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring of natural length 15 cm stretches to 19 cm when a 20 N load hangs from it. The force constant of the spring is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical springs, each of force constant k, are joined end to end (in series) and a load hangs from the lower one. Compared with a single spring carrying the same load, the total extension is
questions.explanation: Each spring carries the full load and stretches by the same amount, so the total extension doubles (the combined constant is k/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cube of side 10 cm and mass 2 kg rests on a table. Taking g = 10 m/s², the pressure it exerts on the table is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A U-tube contains water. Oil of density 800 kg/m³ is poured into one arm and forms a column 10 cm high. The height of water above the oil–water interface in the other arm is
questions.explanation: Pressures balance at the interface level: 800 × 10 = 1,000 × h, so h = 8 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of ice floats in water with 90% of its volume below the surface. The density of ice is approximately
questions.explanation: Fraction submerged = density of ice ÷ density of water, so the density of ice is 0.9 × 1,000 = 900 kg/m³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object weighs 12 N in air and 9 N when fully immersed in water. Its apparent weight when fully immersed in a liquid of relative density 1.2 is
questions.explanation: Upthrust in water = 3 N; in the denser liquid it is 1.2 × 3 = 3.6 N, so the apparent weight is 12 − 3.6 = 8.4 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hydraulic lift has a small piston of area 20 cm² and a large piston of area 400 cm². The force needed on the small piston to raise a 6,000 N car on the large piston is
questions.explanation: Pressure is the same on both pistons: F/20 = 6,000/400, so F = 300 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water rises higher in a narrower capillary tube because
questions.A: a narrower tube holds less water and so is easier to fill
questions.B: the air pressure inside a narrower tube is greater
questions.C: the water inside a narrower tube has a lower density
questions.D: the height of capillary rise is inversely proportional to the tube radius
questions.explanation: h = 2T cos θ/(rρg): the surface-tension force grows with the circumference (∝ r) but the weight of the column grows with r², so a smaller radius supports a taller column.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small drop of water takes a spherical shape because
questions.A: surface tension makes its surface area as small as possible
questions.B: gravity pulls on it equally in every direction
questions.C: the water in a drop has a very high viscosity
questions.D: air pressure squeezes it evenly from all sides
questions.explanation: Surface tension acts to minimise the surface area, and a sphere has the smallest surface area for a given volume.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The elastic limit of a wire is the
questions.A: greatest load it can carry before it finally breaks
questions.B: load at which extension stops being proportional to load
questions.C: point beyond which it does not regain its original length when unloaded
questions.D: load at which the wire begins to melt
questions.explanation: Up to the elastic limit the deformation is temporary; beyond it the wire is permanently stretched.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A brick weighs 30 N and its faces measure 20 cm × 10 cm, 20 cm × 5 cm and 10 cm × 5 cm. The greatest pressure it can exert when resting on a table is
questions.explanation: Pressure is greatest on the smallest face, 10 × 5 = 50 cm² = 0.005 m²: P = 30/0.005 = 6,000 Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A constant-volume gas thermometer reads 80 kPa at the ice point and 109.3 kPa at the steam point. The temperature at which it reads 100 kPa is approximately

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The reading of a clinical thermometer does not fall when it is taken out of the patient's mouth because
questions.A: a constriction in the bore stops the mercury flowing back into the bulb
questions.B: the mercury in the stem cannot contract once it has expanded
questions.C: the bulb is so small that it cools far more slowly than the stem
questions.D: the thick glass of the stem is a very poor conductor of heat
questions.explanation: The narrow kink just above the bulb breaks the mercury thread as it contracts, leaving the reading in the stem until the thermometer is shaken.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Steam at 100 °C causes a more severe burn than the same mass of boiling water at 100 °C because the steam
questions.A: is always at a much higher temperature than the water
questions.B: moves much faster and so strikes the skin harder
questions.C: gives up its latent heat of vaporisation as it condenses
questions.D: penetrates more deeply into the skin than water does
questions.explanation: Each kilogram of steam releases about 2.26 × 10⁶ J on condensing before it even starts to cool as water.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kW heater raises the temperature of 5 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C in 15 minutes. Taking c = 4,200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat lost to the surroundings during this time is
questions.explanation: Supplied: 2,000 × 900 = 1,800,000 J; absorbed by the water: 5 × 4,200 × 80 = 1,680,000 J; the difference, 120,000 J, was lost.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gas at 27 °C is heated at constant pressure until its volume doubles. Its final temperature is
questions.explanation: At constant pressure V ∝ T (kelvin): 300 K → 600 K, which is 600 − 273 = 327 °C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ice at −10 °C is heated steadily until it becomes water at 10 °C. During this process the temperature
questions.A: rises at the same steady rate from start to finish
questions.B: stays constant from start to finish at 0 °C
questions.C: stays constant while the ice melts and rises before and after
questions.D: falls while the ice melts and then rises again
questions.explanation: Heat supplied during melting goes into the latent heat of fusion, so the temperature pauses at 0 °C until all the ice has melted.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal ball just passes through a metal ring at room temperature. If only the ring is heated,
questions.A: the ball still cannot pass because the ring shrinks
questions.B: nothing changes because only the ball's size matters
questions.C: the hole becomes smaller as the metal expands inwards
questions.D: the ball passes through easily because the hole expands
questions.explanation: A hole in a heated plate expands exactly as if it were made of the same metal, so the ring's opening becomes larger.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car radiator uses water as its coolant mainly because water
questions.A: has a high specific heat capacity
questions.B: is cheap and has a low boiling point
questions.C: is a good conductor of electricity
questions.explanation: A high specific heat capacity lets each kilogram of water carry away a large amount of heat for a small rise in temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth through the vacuum of space by
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection need a material medium; only radiation (electromagnetic waves) can cross empty space.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radio wave of wavelength 3 m and a light wave of wavelength 6 × 10⁻⁷ m both travel through a vacuum. Which statement is correct?
questions.C: both travel at the same speed
questions.D: the light wave has the lower frequency
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum; the shorter-wavelength light wave has the higher frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transverse wave on a rope has a frequency of 40 Hz and successive crests are 0.5 m apart. The time the wave takes to travel 100 m along the rope is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two waves of the same frequency and amplitude arrive at a point exactly in phase. The amplitude of the resulting vibration is
questions.B: equal to the amplitude of one wave
questions.C: twice the amplitude of one wave
questions.D: half the amplitude of one wave
questions.explanation: In-phase waves interfere constructively: crest meets crest, so the displacements add to give double the amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stationary (standing) wave differs from a progressive wave in that a stationary wave
questions.B: transfers energy from one place to another
questions.C: has all points vibrating with the same amplitude
questions.D: cannot be produced on a stretched string
questions.explanation: A stationary wave is formed by two identical waves travelling in opposite directions; at the nodes they always cancel, and no energy is carried along.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a stationary wave the distance between a node and the adjacent antinode is 15 cm. The wavelength of the wave is
questions.explanation: Node to neighbouring antinode is a quarter of a wavelength, so λ = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radio station transmits on a wavelength of 300 m. Its frequency is (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The spectral lines in the light from a distant star are found to be shifted towards the red end of the spectrum. This shows that the star is
questions.explanation: By the Doppler effect, light from a receding source is received at a lower frequency (longer wavelength), i.e. shifted towards red.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ambulance siren sounds higher in pitch as the vehicle approaches and lower as it moves away. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Relative motion between the source and the listener changes the frequency received; this is the Doppler effect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In order of decreasing wavelength: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wave is described by y = 0.02 sin(4πx − 100πt), where x and y are in metres and t in seconds. The wavelength of the wave is
questions.explanation: Comparing with y = A sin(kx − ωt): k = 4π = 2π/λ, so λ = 0.5 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water waves of wavelength 2 cm pass through a gap 2 cm wide, and identical waves pass through a gap 20 cm wide. The waves spread out
questions.A: more after passing through the 2 cm gap
questions.C: more after passing through the 20 cm gap
questions.explanation: Diffraction is greatest when the gap width is about equal to the wavelength.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a microwave oven the food is heated because the microwaves
questions.A: are absorbed by water molecules in the food, which then vibrate faster
questions.B: burn the outer surface of the food and the heat then conducts inwards
questions.C: pass straight through the food and heat the metal walls of the oven
questions.D: are reflected repeatedly by the food until it warms up
questions.explanation: Microwaves of about 2.45 GHz are strongly absorbed by water molecules, raising the internal energy of the food throughout.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy hears the echo of his shout from a wall 2 s after shouting. If he walks 165 m closer to the wall and shouts again, the echo returns after (speed of sound = 330 m/s)
questions.explanation: Original distance = 330 × 2/2 = 330 m; new distance = 165 m; echo time = 2 × 165/330 = 1 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound travels faster in water than in air mainly because
questions.A: water has a much greater density than air
questions.B: water is far less compressible than air
questions.C: water is usually colder than the air above it
questions.D: sound waves become transverse in water
questions.explanation: The speed of sound depends on the ratio of elasticity to density; water's very high bulk modulus outweighs its greater density.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A closed pipe and an open pipe have the same length. The fundamental frequency of the closed pipe is
questions.A: the same as that of the open pipe
questions.B: half that of the open pipe
questions.C: twice that of the open pipe
questions.D: a quarter of that of the open pipe
questions.explanation: Fundamental: closed pipe f = v/4L, open pipe f = v/2L, so the closed pipe gives half the frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The quality (timbre) of a note produced by a musical instrument depends on the
questions.A: amplitude of the fundamental vibration alone
questions.B: number and relative strengths of the overtones present
questions.C: speed at which the sound travels through the room
questions.D: loudness with which the note is played
questions.explanation: The same note sounds different on a flute and a guitar because each instrument adds its own mixture of overtones to the fundamental.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sonometer wire 60 cm long is in tune with a fork of frequency 300 Hz. Keeping the tension the same, the length that will be in tune with a 360 Hz fork is
questions.explanation: f ∝ 1/L at constant tension: L = 60 × 300/360 = 50 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stretched wire has a fundamental frequency of 200 Hz. If the tension is increased to nine times its original value with the length unchanged, the fundamental frequency becomes
questions.explanation: f ∝ √T, so multiplying the tension by 9 multiplies the frequency by 3: 600 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the intensity of a sound wave is increased, the property of the sound that increases is its
questions.explanation: Intensity depends on the square of the amplitude and is perceived as loudness; pitch depends on frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: With a certain tuning fork an air column closed at one end resonates first when it is 16 cm long and next when it is 50 cm long. The wavelength of the note is
questions.explanation: Successive resonance lengths differ by λ/2: 50 − 16 = 34 cm, so λ = 68 cm (end correction cancels).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a resonance tube experiment the first and second resonance lengths with a 500 Hz fork are 16 cm and 50 cm. The speed of sound in the air is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 512 Hz fork sounded with a second fork gives 3 beats per second. When a little wax is stuck to the second fork the beats increase to 5 per second. The original frequency of the second fork was
questions.explanation: Wax lowers the second fork's frequency; the beats increased, so its frequency moved further below 512 Hz — it was 512 − 3 = 509 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ultrasound rather than X-rays is used to scan an unborn baby because ultrasound
questions.A: has a much higher frequency than X-rays
questions.B: does not ionise or damage living tissue
questions.C: travels through the body faster than X-rays
questions.D: produces sharper images of the bones
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is a high-frequency sound wave; unlike X-rays it carries no ionising energy and is safe for the developing baby.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fishing trawler's depth finder records an echo 0.8 s after emitting a pulse. Taking the speed of sound in sea water as 1,500 m/s, the water beneath the trawler is
questions.explanation: The pulse travels down and back: depth = 1,500 × 0.8/2 = 600 m deep.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed 40 cm in front of a convex (diverging) mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is
questions.A: 13.3 cm behind the mirror, virtual, erect and diminished
questions.B: 40 cm in front of the mirror, real, inverted and same size
questions.C: 13.3 cm in front of the mirror, real, inverted and diminished
questions.D: 40 cm behind the mirror, virtual, erect and magnified
questions.explanation: With f = −20 cm: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 − 1/40 = −3/40, so v = −13.3 cm — a virtual, erect image one-third the size.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm is used to throw a sharp image of a lamp onto a screen 60 cm from the mirror. The lamp must be placed at

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light inside glass of refractive index 1.5 meets the glass–air surface at an angle of incidence of 45°. The ray is
questions.A: refracted away from the normal into the air
questions.B: totally internally reflected back into the glass
questions.C: refracted towards the normal into the air
questions.explanation: sin C = 1/1.5 gives a critical angle of about 42°; 45° exceeds this, so no light escapes and the ray is totally reflected.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coin at the bottom of a beaker of water appears to be raised. This is because light from the coin
questions.A: is totally reflected at the surface of the water
questions.B: bends away from the normal as it leaves the water
questions.C: bends towards the normal as it leaves the water
questions.D: travels faster in the water than it does in air
questions.explanation: Refraction away from the normal on leaving the denser medium makes the rays appear to come from a point higher than the coin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens forms a real image the same size as the object when the object is placed
questions.C: between the principal focus and the lens
questions.explanation: With u = 2f the image is also at 2f, real, inverted and the same size (magnification 1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A slide projector uses a converging lens to throw a large image of a slide onto a distant screen. The slide must be placed
questions.A: between the lens and its principal focus
questions.B: between f and 2f from the lens
questions.explanation: An object between f and 2f gives a real, inverted and magnified image beyond 2f on the other side — the image is then focused on the screen.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The image formed on the film of a simple camera is
questions.explanation: The object is far beyond 2f, so the converging lens forms a small, real, inverted image just beyond its focal point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A short-sighted person cannot see distant objects clearly because the image of a distant object is formed
questions.C: on the retina but upside down
questions.explanation: The eyeball is too long or the lens too powerful, so parallel rays converge before the retina; a diverging lens corrects the defect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: White light passes first through a red filter and then through a green filter. The light that emerges is
questions.explanation: The red filter transmits only red light, which the green filter absorbs, so nothing passes through both.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spectacle lens has a power of −2.5 D. It is a
questions.A: converging lens of focal length 40 cm
questions.B: diverging lens of focal length 40 cm
questions.C: converging lens of focal length 25 cm
questions.D: diverging lens of focal length 2.5 cm
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/2.5 m = 40 cm; the negative sign means a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The image in a pinhole camera becomes sharper but dimmer when
questions.explanation: A smaller hole lets through a narrower cone of rays from each point of the object (sharper) but less light overall (dimmer).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diver under water looks up and sees the surface above her act like a mirror, except for a bright circular window directly overhead. The mirror-like region is produced by
questions.A: refraction of light from the air into the water at small angles
questions.B: total internal reflection of light striking the surface beyond the critical angle
questions.C: diffraction of light round the edge of the bright circular window
questions.D: dispersion of sunlight into colours at the water surface
questions.explanation: Light from below the surface that meets it at more than the critical angle (about 49° for water) cannot escape and is reflected back down, so the surface looks silvery outside the window.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Their combined resistance is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of resistance 12 Ω is cut into three equal pieces which are then connected in parallel. The resistance of the combination is
questions.explanation: Each piece is 4 Ω; three 4 Ω resistors in parallel give 4/3 = 1.33 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Bulbs rated 40 W, 240 V and 100 W, 240 V are connected in series across a 240 V supply. Which bulb glows brighter?
questions.A: the 40 W bulb, because it has the larger resistance and carries the same current
questions.B: the 100 W bulb, because its higher power rating means it always glows brighter
questions.C: both glow equally brightly, because the same current flows through both
questions.D: the 100 W bulb, because it draws a larger current than the 40 W bulb
questions.explanation: In series the current is the same in both; power = I²R, so the bulb with the larger resistance (the 40 W bulb, R = V²/P) dissipates more power.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1.5 kW electric iron is used for 2 hours a day for 30 days. At ₦60 per kilowatt-hour the cost of the electricity used is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a wire is R. If the wire is replaced by one of the same material and length but twice the diameter, the new resistance is
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A and doubling the diameter multiplies the area by four, so the resistance falls to R/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is short-circuited by a thick copper wire of negligible resistance. The current that flows is
questions.explanation: I = E/r = 1.5/0.5 = 3 A; the internal resistance alone limits the current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical cells, each of e.m.f. 2 V and internal resistance 1 Ω, are connected in parallel across a 1.5 Ω resistor. The current in the resistor is
questions.explanation: In parallel the e.m.f. stays 2 V and the internal resistance halves to 0.5 Ω: I = 2/(0.5 + 1.5) = 1 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 200 V. The charge stored on it is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In house wiring the fuse for an appliance is always placed in the
questions.explanation: When a fuse in the live wire blows it disconnects the appliance from the high-voltage side; in the neutral wire the appliance would remain live after the fuse blew.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student mistakenly connects a voltmeter in series with a bulb and a cell. The bulb does not light because the voltmeter
questions.A: has a very high resistance and allows almost no current to flow
questions.B: has a very low resistance and short-circuits the bulb
questions.C: reverses the direction of the current in the circuit
questions.D: uses up the whole e.m.f. of the cell as heat
questions.explanation: A voltmeter is designed to draw negligible current; in series it acts almost like an open switch.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A step-up transformer has 200 turns in its primary coil and 4,000 turns in its secondary. If the primary current is 2 A, the secondary current (assuming 100% efficiency) is
questions.explanation: Ip Np = Is Ns for an ideal transformer: Is = 2 × 200/4,000 = 0.1 A — the voltage goes up 20 times, the current down 20 times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 20 kW of power is sent along cables of total resistance 5 Ω. When the transmission voltage is 10 kV, the power lost as heat in the cables is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil of 50 turns and area 0.02 m² has its plane perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.4 T. The field is reduced to zero in 0.1 s. The average e.m.f. induced in the coil is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer does not work with a steady direct current in its primary coil because
questions.A: a direct current cannot flow through a coil of many turns
questions.B: a steady current produces a steady flux, which induces no e.m.f.
questions.C: the soft-iron core becomes permanently magnetised by d.c.
questions.D: a direct current has no potential difference across it
questions.explanation: An e.m.f. is induced only while the magnetic flux linking the secondary is changing; a constant current gives a constant flux.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric motor and a generator are alike in construction. The difference is that in a motor
questions.A: electrical energy is converted to mechanical energy
questions.B: mechanical energy is converted to electrical energy
questions.explanation: A motor is driven by a current and turns; a generator is turned and produces a current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The back e.m.f. in a running electric motor
questions.A: increases the current drawn when the motor runs faster
questions.B: opposes the applied voltage and limits the current as the motor speeds up
questions.C: is greatest when the motor is stationary
questions.D: is produced by the split-ring commutator
questions.explanation: The rotating coil acts as a generator; its induced e.m.f. opposes the supply, which is why a motor draws a large current only at start-up.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnetic compass is placed directly below a horizontal wire that runs north–south. When a large current is switched on in the wire, the needle
questions.A: continues to point towards magnetic north as before
questions.B: is deflected sideways towards the east or the west
questions.C: swings round to point vertically downwards
questions.D: loses its magnetism while the current flows
questions.explanation: Oersted's experiment: the current produces a magnetic field in circles round the wire, which is east–west below the wire and turns the needle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle moving parallel to the lines of a magnetic field experiences
questions.C: a force along the field direction
questions.D: a force opposite to the field direction
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is F = qvB sin θ; when the velocity is parallel to the field, θ = 0 and the force is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron (charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) moving at 2 × 10⁶ m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of 0.5 T experiences a force of

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following metals is NOT attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron, nickel and cobalt are ferromagnetic; copper is not attracted by a magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of the alternating e.m.f. produced by a simple generator is doubled when
questions.A: the number of turns on the coil is doubled
questions.B: the speed of rotation of the coil is doubled
questions.C: the strength of the magnetic field is doubled
questions.D: the area of the coil is doubled
questions.explanation: One revolution produces one complete cycle, so the output frequency equals the rotation rate; the other changes alter only the peak e.m.f.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnetic field is described as uniform when its field lines are
questions.B: curved round the poles of a magnet
questions.D: all pointing towards the north pole
questions.explanation: Equally spaced parallel lines mean the field has the same strength and direction everywhere, as between the flat poles of a horseshoe magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive nuclide has a half-life of 3 hours. The fraction of the original nuclei that has decayed after 9 hours is
questions.explanation: 9 hours is three half-lives, so 1/8 of the nuclei remain and 7/8 have decayed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the fission reaction ²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ¹⁴¹₅₆Ba + ⁹²₃₆Kr + x ¹₀n, the value of x is
questions.explanation: Mass numbers balance: 235 + 1 = 141 + 92 + x, so x = 3 neutrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The nuclide ²¹⁰₈₂Pb decays by beta emission. The daughter nuclide has
questions.explanation: Beta emission turns a neutron into a proton: the atomic number rises by one and the mass number is unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Geiger counter registers 40 counts per minute from background radiation alone, and 680 counts per minute with a radioactive source present. After two half-lives of the source it will register about
questions.explanation: Source count = 680 − 40 = 640; after two half-lives it is 160, plus the constant background of 40 gives 200.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Nuclear fusion, the process that powers the Sun, involves
questions.A: the splitting of heavy nuclei into lighter ones
questions.B: the joining of light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus
questions.C: the emission of alpha particles from uranium nuclei
questions.D: the capture of electrons by protons
questions.explanation: In the Sun hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium, releasing energy from the loss of mass (E = mc²).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which radiation from a radioactive source is NOT deflected by electric or magnetic fields?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are uncharged electromagnetic waves; alpha (positive) and beta (negative) particles are deflected in opposite directions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear reactor the control rods are made of boron or cadmium because these materials
questions.D: reflect neutrons back into the core
questions.explanation: Lowering the rods removes neutrons from the chain reaction and slows it; raising them speeds it up.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The moderator (graphite or heavy water) in a nuclear reactor is used to
questions.A: absorb the excess neutrons and stop the reaction
questions.B: slow the fast neutrons so they cause further fission
questions.C: carry the heat away from the hot fuel rods
questions.D: shield the workers from the radiation produced
questions.explanation: Slow (thermal) neutrons are far more likely to be captured by uranium-235 and cause fission than fast ones.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass defect of a nucleus is 0.1 u. Taking 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the binding energy of the nucleus is approximately

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioisotope chosen as a medical tracer should have
questions.A: a very long half-life so that it remains active in the body for years
questions.B: a short half-life and gamma emission that can be detected outside the body
questions.C: a long half-life and alpha emission that stays inside the body tissue
questions.D: no radiation at all so that the patient is not harmed in any way
questions.explanation: Gamma rays escape the body to be detected by a camera, and a short half-life keeps the patient's total dose small.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sample contains 8 × 10²⁰ atoms of a radioactive isotope with a half-life of 5 days. The number of undecayed atoms left after 15 days is
questions.explanation: 15 days is three half-lives: 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 × 10²⁰ atoms.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Alpha particles are more strongly ionising than beta particles because alpha particles
questions.A: move much faster and so hit more atoms every second
questions.B: carry more charge and move more slowly, so they ionise more atoms per cm
questions.C: are electromagnetic waves that penetrate deep into matter
questions.D: have no charge and so collide directly with the nuclei of atoms
questions.explanation: The doubly charged, heavy, relatively slow alpha particle pulls electrons off almost every atom it passes, which is also why its range is so short.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light whose frequency is below the threshold frequency of a metal falls on its surface. The metal
questions.A: emits electrons only if the light is bright enough
questions.B: emits no electrons however bright the light is
questions.C: emits electrons after a short time delay
questions.D: emits electrons with very high kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Each photon has energy hf, which is less than the work function; no single photon can free an electron, whatever the intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The stopping potential for the photoelectrons emitted from a metal is 1.2 V. The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons is (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal with a work function of 2.0 eV is illuminated with violet light of wavelength 400 nm. Taking hc = 1,240 eV nm, the fastest photoelectrons leave with a kinetic energy of
questions.explanation: Photon energy = hc/λ = 1,240/400 = 3.1 eV; KE_max = 3.1 − 2.0 = 1.1 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Silicon doped with boron (a Group 3 element) becomes a semiconductor in which the majority charge carriers are
questions.explanation: Boron has one electron fewer than silicon, leaving a vacancy (hole) in the bonding; the material is p-type.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bridge rectifier of four diodes is fed with a 50 Hz alternating supply. The ripple frequency of its full-wave rectified output is
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectification turns both halves of each cycle positive, giving two pulses per cycle: 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a common-emitter transistor amplifier, a small change in the base current produces
questions.A: a large change in the collector current
questions.B: no change in the collector current
questions.C: an equal change in the collector current
questions.D: a large change in the base voltage only
questions.explanation: The collector current is β times the base current (β typically 50–300), which is the basis of current amplification.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transistor has a current gain of 100. When its base current is 20 μA the collector current is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A security alarm should sound (output 1) when either the door sensor or the window sensor, or both, is triggered (input 1). The logic gate needed is
questions.explanation: An OR gate gives an output of 1 when at least one of its inputs is 1; an AND gate would need both sensors to be triggered at once.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a cathode-ray oscilloscope the electron beam is produced by
questions.A: photoelectric emission from a cold cathode
questions.B: thermionic emission from a heated cathode
questions.explanation: A heated filament (cathode) boils off electrons, which are then accelerated and focused by the anodes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: X-rays and gamma rays are both electromagnetic waves. The essential difference is that X-rays
questions.A: have much longer wavelengths than any gamma rays and less energy
questions.B: come from electron transitions or stopped electrons, not from the nucleus
questions.C: cannot penetrate matter as gamma rays do and are stopped by paper
questions.D: carry an electric charge whereas gamma rays are always neutral
questions.explanation: Gamma rays originate in the nucleus; X-rays are produced outside it, by fast electrons striking a target or by inner-shell electron transitions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a moving particle is halved when its
questions.explanation: λ = h/p, so the wavelength is inversely proportional to the momentum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light-emitting diode (LED) gives out light only when it is
questions.explanation: Current flows through the junction only in forward bias, and the recombining charge carriers release their energy as light.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, an electron that moves from the second energy level down to the first
questions.A: absorbs a photon whose energy equals the gap between the levels
questions.B: emits a photon whose energy equals the gap between the levels
questions.C: loses part of its electric charge to the nucleus
questions.D: gains kinetic energy without any radiation being emitted
questions.explanation: Falling to a lower level releases energy as a photon of frequency f = (E₂ − E₁)/h; jumping up requires a photon to be absorbed.
